notes: Identity verified from the supplied canonical text: title Impact of APOE on the Healthy Aging Brain: A Voxel-Based MRI and DTI Study; authors Robyn A Honea, Eric Vidoni, Amith Harsha, Jeffrey M Burns; DOI 10.3233/JAD-2009-1163; final publication J Alzheimers Dis. 2009 Nov;18(3):553–564. PMC author manuscript, including methods, results, Tables 1 and 2, discussion and references; primary research report, not merely an abstract. No PDF supplied; no page-layout verification available. No original locator and only a paper-level description are supplied. The article reports multiple cognitive, VBM, DTI and lifestyle analyses; no unique target can be selected. Common sample candidate only: the VBM methods explicitly state analysis for 53 subjects after excluding eleven for movement artifact/inhomogeneity. Demographics explicitly identify 14 carriers and 39 noncarriers; DTI methods report 53 FA images. Participant role, not voxels or brain clusters. Clinical exclusions include neurological disease other than AD, ischemic heart disease, significant mental illness, diabetes or other impairing systemic illness; all analyzed participants had CDR=0. No N calculated from degrees of freedom and no group-sum calculation used. Because the requested row/test is unresolved, these sample counts remain candidates for parent field-scope review and are not entered as a verified row-specific analytic N. Table 1 contains age, gender, education, family history, whole brain volume, whole gray volume, whole white matter volume, standardized cognitive score, PASE, ADL, VO2lean and physical performance test. It reports means (SD) or percentages/counts and a significance column, not a unique omnibus effect selected by the supplied broad description. Candidate standardized cognitive score comparison has noncarrier mean 0.08 (SD 0.42), carrier mean −0.20 (SD 0.53), p=0.047; age comparison has p=0.588. These examples demonstrate multiple possible rows; neither is assigned as the target. The locator suffix N1 does not identify a named outcome or test in the supplied text. Table 2 reports multiple distinct VBM contrasts/regions, with Z score (not an effect-size conversion) and uncorrected p, plus parenthetical corrected entries. Decreases: L lingual/parahippocampal gyrus/precuneus Z=3.52, p<0.001; R inferior parietal cortex Z=3.25, p=0.001; L superior frontal cortex Z=3.14, p=0.001; L angular/supramarginal gyrus Z=3.14, p=0.001; L amygdala Z=3.11, p=0.001; R precuneus Z=3.01, p=0.001; SVC hippocampus/amygdala printed Z score 3.11 (3.56), p 0.001 (0.049). Increases: R medial frontal gyrus Z=3.82, p<0.001; L middle temporal gyrus Z=3.50, p<0.001; L middle occipital gyrus Z=3.16, p=0.001; R inferior frontal gyrus Z=3.14, p=0.001; R precuneus Z=3.13, p=0.001; R hippocampus Z=3.12, p=0.001; SVC hippocampus/amygdala Z=3.12, p 0.001 (0.333). Parentheses retained as printed, with table footnote identifying corrected FWE values. No unique regional contrast supplied. DTI candidate: left parahippocampal gyrus FA decrease p<0.001 uncorrected; no corrected significance at p<0.05.
